Experimental Nuclear Reaction Data (EXFOR)

Remake sketch · seed data

Layout and behavior of nds.iaea.org/exfor (software 2026-08-28) · the entries below are made-up seed data, not real measurements

The EXFOR library contains an extensive compilation of experimental nuclear reaction data. The retrieval system provides data search, output to various formats, plotting and comparison to ENDF, re-normalization of old data to new standards, calculating data for inverse reactions and kinematics, and correlation matrices from partial uncertainties.

This sketch holds seed entries. The real version reads 27,116 entries, 223,615 subentries and 19,439,354 data rows from the NSR lake.

Recipe for the real version (a prompt for the build window) 
Build NSRgpt's EXFOR search: a working remake of nds.iaea.org/exfor inside NSRgpt, over the data already in s3://nsr-lake-613473203863 (AWS profile nysgpt-new, us-east-2). The layout and behavior to match are in ~/Code/nsrgpt/docs/sketches/2026-11-07-exfor-replica.html (form, options, "?" pickers, results, plot).

Rules (Brendan's, standing)
1. Efficiency Voice: ~/Code/nsrgpt/docs/sketches/2026-11-06-efficiency-voice.html. Read it first; report in it.
2. No commits or pushes until Brendan says so. No subagents.
3. The Mac has 8 GB: no python3 on it, AWS CLI one call at a time. Unzipping, loading, parsing and calculating run on AWS (a box or Lambda), output in S3.
4. The repo stays a thin UI layer. Data and heavy work live in the lake and behind the API. Pages load instantly; data loads after.
5. Reuse NSRgpt's components (blocks, Row/Section, the sidebar fold, the kebab). Plain labels.

Sources already in the lake
- All of EXFOR: raw/iaea/2026-11-07/cdroms/dwn/x4sqlite-20251105-c.zip (X4Pro, one SQLite database, Nov 2025). Newer entries: raw/github/IAEA-NDS/EXFOR-JSON-File (J4, current to 2026-10-28), EXFOR-Entry-File (X4), EXFOR-C4-File, EXFOR-Plot-File (CX4). EXFOR C5 v4 and x5json in cdroms/dwn/.
- Picker dictionaries: raw/github/IAEA-NDS/exfor_dictionary.
- CINDA: cdroms/dwn/x4apps-2021-12-15.zip and raw/iaea/2026-11-07/…/exfor-master/cinda/.
- IAEA's code: x4apps-2021-12-15 (the retrieval system: re-normalization, inverse reactions, kinematics, ENDF comparison), x4pro1-20230630-mini (X4Pro codes), raw/github/IAEA-NDS/ForEXy (format converters, current), raw/github/IAEA-NDS/neutron-standards-database (standards for re-normalization).
- Evaluated libraries for comparison: raw/nndc/2026-11-07/endf-releases/ (ENDF/B-II to B-VIII.1), raw/iaea/2026-11-07/ (JEFF-4.0/3.3, JENDL-5, CENDL-3.2, ROSFOND-2010, BROND-3.1, FENDL-3.2), raw/openmc/2026-11-07/ (HDF5, easiest to plot).

Steps
1. Parse: on an AWS box, unzip X4Pro, read its schema, and write entries, subentries, reactions, data rows, references, authors and institutes as Parquet in lake/exfor/2026-11/ (the parsed layer). Register the tables in the Glue database nsr. Check counts against J4 (27,116 entries, 223,615 subentries, 19,439,354 data rows) and add what J4 has that X4Pro lacks.
2. Dictionaries: targets, reactions, quantities, products, institutes, countries as tables. They drive the "?" pickers.
3. Serving tables: one row per subentry with every search field (target, reaction, quantity, product, energy min and max, authors, year, last modified, accession, NSR key number), and the data rows per subentry for plots.
4. API: a Lambda behind a cache (search, subentry data, outputs) reading the serving tables. Cache responses by query.
5. UI: /exfor in NSRgpt with the sketch's form, options, pickers and results, in NSRgpt's design system. The page shell is static; results load after.
6. Outputs: X4, C4, C5, JSON and CSV, from the files held and ForEXy.
7. Plot and ENDF comparison: evaluated curves from OpenMC HDF5 (or endf-parserpy on the ENDF-6 files) over the measured points, any library.
8. Calculations: run IAEA's own code from x4apps and the X4Pro codes on the box for re-normalization (with the current neutron standards), inverse reactions, kinematics and correlation matrices. Port a calculation into the API only after its results match.
9. Verify: 50 reference requests spread across targets, reactions and quantities. Same entries, same points, same re-normalized values as nds.iaea.org/exfor (read through the proxy box, or by Brendan). List every difference.
10. Link: NSR key numbers to EXFOR entries (nsr_exfor and the X4Pro references) so chat cites both.

Done means
1. /exfor answers the 50 reference requests the same way nds.iaea.org/exfor does.
2. The parsed and serving tables, the API and its cache are in the lake and AWS.
3. README and /pipeline updated (EXFOR measured data moves from planned to live).
4. A final report in Efficiency Voice.
